newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise sharply, LVMH rebounds.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise sharply, LVMH rebounds.

text.p: French stocks rose sharply on Friday as investors gave the new Socialist-led government the benefit of the doubt after what was viewed as a prudent keynote policy speech by Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on Thursday.
The CAC-40 index closed up 17.41 points, or 0.64 percent, at 2,757.10. The CAC-40 June futures contract rose 19 to 2,749.

"The markets keep giving Jospin the benefit of the doubt," said a broker. He added that the speech contained no unpleasant surprises, although many questions were left unanswered, notably on how the government would finance its spending plans.
On the week, the CAC finished down 1.83 percent.
"There are some who think the market could fall and others who don't feel there's much to worry about," a trader said.

The bourse was underpinned on Friday by the firmness in the dollar and franc, gains in Frankfurt and an early rise on Wall Street. Shares in retail and building groups rose on the government's measures to boost consumption and provide more housing.
The CAC index was also boosted by a rebound in LVMH, which finished up 4.79 percent, recovering the ground lost since it began buying up Grand Met stock this week.

Some analysts sympathise with LVMH Chairman Bernard Arnault's criticisms of the planned Guinness-Grand Met merger, but others are concerned, saying he risks taking on a lot of debt in his effort to thwart the deal.
LVMH has paid around 790 million pounds for a 6.3 percent stake in Grand Met and it is expected to buy more Grand Met stock.

* Alcatel Alsthom closed up 3.22 percent in heavy turnover of 1.2 million shares after chairman Serge Tchuruk's forecast at the annual general meeting on Thursday that operating profit would more than double this year.
* Construction materials company Lapeyre rose 4.99 percent, helped by the government's measures on housing.
* Sodexho finished up 4.17 percent after reporting 1996/97 H1 net attrib 269 million francs against 213.31 million. It forecast full-year net of around 535 million.
